The noun proceeding refers to a formal, official action or series of steps — something that happens within a structured, rule-governed framework, such as a court of law, an official meeting, or an organized institution.

The word always carries a sense of seriousness and structure. It does not belong to the world of casual, everyday life. You would never say "the proceedings of our lunch" — that would sound odd. The word belongs to courtrooms, conferences, and formal gatherings.

You will encounter this word far more often in its plural form: "proceedings." The singular — "a proceeding" — appears mainly in legal writing. The plural — "proceedings" — is used across all contexts.

Both are grammatically correct, but knowing this will help you recognize the word in the wild.
Meaning 1 — A legal action or the steps of a legal process (the most common and important meaning)

In law, a proceeding (or proceedings) refers to an official action carried out through a legal system — such as a trial, a hearing, an investigation, a lawsuit, or any formal step taken by a court or governmental body.

When the legal system begins doing something official — filing a case, holding a hearing, conducting a trial — all of those actions together, or each individual one, can be called a "proceeding."

Examples:

  • "The judge opened the proceedings at 9 a.m." — the official formal activities of the court session had begun.
  • "Criminal proceedings were initiated against the suspect." — the official legal process of prosecution had started.
  • "The bankruptcy proceedings lasted three months." — the entire official legal process of handling the bankruptcy case took three months.
  • "The proceeding was adjourned until next week." — the single legal session or hearing was postponed.

Common phrases you will see:

  • legal proceedings
  • criminal proceedings
  • court proceedings
  • civil proceedings
  • bankruptcy proceedings
  • disciplinary proceedings
  • immigration proceedings

The key point: a "proceeding" in law is not a casual conversation or informal discussion. It is an official, structured action with rules, participants who have defined roles (judge, lawyer, defendant), and real legal consequences.
Meaning 2 — The events that take place at a formal gathering or meeting

"Proceedings" also refers to the things that happen at an organized, formal event — such as a ceremony, a committee meeting, a conference session, or any official gathering. Here, the word is essentially a formal way of saying "what went on" or "the events of the occasion."

Examples:

  • "She watched the proceedings from the back of the hall." — she watched everything that was happening at the formal event.
  • "The proceedings were interrupted by a fire alarm." — the activities of the meeting or session were disrupted.
  • "The chairman presided over the proceedings." — he was in charge of how the event unfolded and was conducted.

Note: in this meaning, "proceedings" refers to the actual, live events as they happen or happened — not a document or record of those events.
Meaning 3 — The published record of a conference or academic meeting

In academic, scientific, and professional communities, "proceedings" has a very specific meaning: an official publication — a book or document — that collects and records the research papers, talks, and presentations given at a conference or symposium.

Think of it as the "official report" of a conference. Researchers submit papers to a conference, those papers are presented and discussed, and they are then collected and published together as the "proceedings" of that conference. It essentially becomes the permanent written record of what was contributed and discussed at that event.

Examples:

  • "Her paper was published in the Proceedings of the International Conference on Artificial Intelligence." — her paper became part of the official published collection from that conference.
  • "The proceedings of last year's symposium are available on the website." — the published record of what was presented at the symposium can be found there.
  • "He has had three papers accepted in major conference proceedings." — his research has been included in the official publications of three major conferences.

If you ever see something like "Proceedings of the Royal Society" or "ACM Conference Proceedings," this is exactly what it refers to — a published collection of academic work from a formal gathering.
Meaning 4 — A particular action or course of action (less common, somewhat old-fashioned)

More rarely, "a proceeding" (singular) can refer to a particular action or a specific way of doing something, especially when it is part of a larger sequence of events. You are unlikely to hear this in everyday modern speech, but you may encounter it in older or very formal writing.

Example:

  • "It was a strange proceeding — nobody could understand why she had done it that way." — it was a strange action or course of behavior that nobody could make sense of.

You do not need to use this meaning yourself, but it is good to recognize it if you come across it.
The thread that connects all meanings

Across all its meanings, "proceeding" always implies:

Formality — it happens within an official, structured framework, not in a casual setting.

Process — it involves steps and actions unfolding in a particular order or sequence, usually following established rules.

Institutional context — it belongs to the world of law, academia, governance, or organized formal events.

If you strip it down to its simplest essence: a proceeding is something that happens officially and formally, within a system that has rules and structure.
How to tell which meaning applies when you encounter the word

When you read or hear "proceedings," ask yourself: what kind of context is this?

  • If it's a courtroom, lawsuit, trial, or legal document → it means a legal action or legal process.
  • If it's describing what is happening at a live event or meeting → it means the events or activities of that gathering.
  • If it's a book or publication from a conference → it means the official published record of that conference.
  • If it's in old or very formal writing describing a specific action → it means that particular action or course of behavior.

The word itself rarely causes ambiguity because the surrounding context almost always makes the meaning obvious.
